docs.title: Checkstyle Spellcheck Extension
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for checkstyle-spellcheck, a high-performance Checkstyle extension that validates the spelling of Java identifiers across all declaration AST nodes.

Powered by the Apache Lucene Hunspell morphology engine, this extension brings industrial-grade spellchecking to your Java builds with zero external configuration required out of the box.

docs.title: Why Checkstyle Spellcheck?
docs.text:
• Catch typos before production: Typos in public APIs, method names, database entities, and record components stay in codebases forever due to backwards compatibility.
  • Zero-Config English Default: Ships with embedded en_US Hunspell dictionary (en_US.aff and en_US.dic) as classpath resources.
  • Morphology-Aware: Understands prefixes, suffixes, compound words, and inflections using Hunspell's linguistic production rules.
  • Blazing Fast: Employs an in-memory lock-free word cache (ConcurrentHashMap) to achieve $O(1)$ amortized validation speed across massive enterprise codebases.
  • Clean Single Whitelist: Project-controlled whitelist for domain jargon, abbreviations, and technical acronyms.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
public class UserService {
    // Checkstyle flags: 'adress' -> Misspelled word
    private String userAdress;

    // Checkstyle flags: 'namme' -> Misspelled word
    public void printNamme() {
        System.out.println(userAdress);
    }
}

[WARN] UserService.java:3:20: Identifier 'userAdress' contains misspelled word 'adress'. [IdentifierSpellingCheck]
[WARN] UserService.java:6:17: Identifier 'printNamme' contains misspelled word 'namme'. [IdentifierSpellingCheck]

docs.title: 1. Overview & Objectives
docs.text: The Checkstyle Spellcheck Extension (checkstyle-spellcheck) is an external Checkstyle module that inspects Java Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) to validate the spelling of identifiers (classes, methods, variables, parameters, record components, enum constants, annotations) against an embedded or custom Hunspell dictionary and an optional project whitelist.

docs.title: Core Design Goals
docs.text:
1. Lightweight Core Checkstyle: Maintained as an independent extension JAR ( io.github.praveen7294:checkstyle-spellcheck) discovered via Checkstyle SPI (checkstyle_packages.xml).
  2. Zero-Configuration Out-of-the-Box: Ships with standard en_US Hunspell dictionary (en_US.aff and en_US.dic) embedded as classpath resources.
  3. High-Throughput AST Processing: Analyzes hundreds of thousands of identifiers across large codebases in milliseconds with minimal CPU and memory overhead.
  4. Morphology-Aware Validation: Leverages Apache Lucene Hunspell to understand English morphology (affixes, prefixes, suffixes, compound rules) rather than brittle, flat word lists.
  5. Resilient Lexical Splitting: Accurately decomposes camelCase, PascalCase, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, acronyms ( HTTPServer, JSONResponse), and digits (sha256Hash, param1).

docs.title: 2. High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
The system divides responsibilities into four distinct layers:

graph TD
    A["Java Source File"] --> B["Checkstyle TreeWalker"]
    B --> C["IdentifierSpellingCheck (AST Visitor)"]
    C --> D["IdentifierWordSplitter"]
    D -->|"Normalized Words (List<String>)"| E["SpellChecker"]

    subgraph "SpellChecker Validation Pipeline"
        E --> F{"Tier 1: Whitelist Set"}
        F -- "Found (O(1))" --> G["VALID"]
        F -- "Not Found" --> H{"Tier 2: Fast Word Cache"}
        H -- "Cache Hit (True/False)" --> G
        H -- "Cache Miss" --> I["Tier 3: Lucene Hunspell Engine"]
        I -->|"hunspell.spell(word)"| J{"Valid Morphological Word?"}
        J -- "Yes" --> K["Record in Cache (Valid)"] --> G
        J -- "No" --> L["Record in Cache (Invalid)"] --> M["VIOLATION"]
    end

    M --> N["Checkstyle Log (AST Line:Column)"]

docs.title: The Power of .dic and .aff
docs.text:
Unlike static word lists that require storing every form of a word (write, writes, writing, written), Hunspell uses two coordinated files:

  • .dic (Dictionary File): Base stems associated with morphological flags (write/SDR).
  • .aff (Affix Rule File): Linguistic production rules (prefixes, suffixes, inflections, replacement tables).

docs.title: Engine Components in Lucene 10
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class Dictionary {
        +FST prefixes
        +FST suffixes
        +WordStorage words
        +Dictionary(InputStream aff, List~InputStream~ dic, boolean ignoreCase, SortingStrategy strategy)
    }

    class Hunspell {
        +spell(String word) boolean
        +Hunspell(Dictionary dictionary)
    }

    class SortingStrategy {
        +inMemory()$ SortingStrategy
    }

    Dictionary <-- Hunspell : reads
    SortingStrategy --> Dictionary : compiles in-memory
  1. org.apache.lucene.analysis.hunspell.Dictionary (Heavyweight, Immutable):
    • Parses .aff rules and compiles prefixes/suffixes into Finite State Transducers (FSTs).
    • Compiles .dic words using SortingStrategy.inMemory().
    • Compiled once per check configuration in finishLocalSetup(). Strictly read-only and thread-safe.
  2. org.apache.lucene.analysis.hunspell.Hunspell (Lightweight Query Engine):
    • Built on top of Dictionary.
    • Ultra-fast $O(\text{word length})$ lookups via spell(String).

docs.title: 1. Checkstyle Lifecycle Integration (finishLocalSetup)
docs.text:
Checkstyle instantiates IdentifierSpellingCheck as a @StatelessCheck. In finishLocalSetup(), the SpellChecker is compiled once:

  • For zero-config runs: It streams en_US.aff and en_US.dic from embedded classpath resources.
  • For custom dictionary runs: It streams external files from disk.
  • Across all files audited in a single run, dictionary compilation happens exactly once.

docs.title: 2. Three-Tier Validation Pipeline
docs.text: Tier Component Time Complexity Purpose Tier 1 Project Whitelist (Set<String>) $O(1)$ Immediate bypass for project acronyms and jargon (dto, dao, uuid, regex). Tier 2 Fast Word Cache (ConcurrentHashMap<String, Boolean>) $O(1)$ Caches both positive (true) and negative (false) lookups for common identifiers (user, name, get, set, id). Tier 3 Lucene Hunspell.spell() $O(\text{length})$ Traverses affix trees and root tables for words not yet seen. The result is automatically recorded in Tier 2.

docs.title: 5. Identifier Word Splitting Pipeline
docs.text:
Java identifiers combine multiple words using varying conventions. IdentifierWordSplitter normalizes identifiers before validation:

flowchart LR
    A["Raw AST Identifier (e.g. 'processSha256Hashe')"] --> B["1. Split by underscores & digits ('_+', '\\d+')"]
    B --> C["Segments: ['processSha', 'Hashe']"]
    C --> D["2. CamelCase & Acronym boundary regexes"]
    D --> E["Words: ['process', 'Sha', 'Hashe']"]
    E --> F["3. Case normalization (toLowerCase)"]
    F --> G["Final: ['process', 'sha', 'hashe']"]

docs.title: Splitting Specification
docs.text:
• Underscores: Separated by Pattern.compile("_+").
  • Digits: Separated by Pattern.compile("\\d+").
  • Lower to Upper (Camel/Pascal): Pattern.compile("(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])").
  • Acronym Boundaries: Pattern.compile("(?<=[A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])") (HTTPServer → http, server).
  • Normalization: All emitted words are normalized to lowercase (Locale.ROOT).

docs.title: 6. Resource Resolution
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["finishLocalSetup()"] --> B{"dictionaryFile and affixFile provided?"}
    B -- "No / Blank" --> C["Load embedded default en_US dictionary from Classpath (/io/github/praveen7294/checkstyle/spellcheck/dictionaries/en_US.*)"]
    B -- "Yes" --> D["Load external files via FileInputStream"]

    A --> E{"whitelist path provided?"}
    E -- "No / Blank" --> F["Empty Whitelist (Collections.emptySet())"]
    E -- "Yes" --> G["Load and parse custom whitelist.txt"]

docs.title: IdentifierSpellingCheck.java
docs.text:
• Extends AbstractCheck.
  • Annotated with @StatelessCheck.
  • Audits 11 AST tokens:
    • Types: CLASS_DEF, INTERFACE_DEF, RECORD_DEF, ENUM_DEF, ANNOTATION_DEF
    • Members: METHOD_DEF, VARIABLE_DEF, PARAMETER_DEF, RECORD_COMPONENT_DEF, ANNOTATION_FIELD_DEF, ENUM_CONSTANT_DEF
  • Properties:
    • dictionaryFile (String)
    • affixFile (String)
    • whitelist (String)

docs.title: SpellChecker.java
docs.text:
• Thread-safe validation engine.
  • Constructors:
    • SpellChecker() (Embedded default dictionary, no whitelist)
    • SpellChecker(String whitelistPath) (Embedded default dictionary + whitelist)
    • SpellChecker(String dicPath, String affPath, String whitelistPath) (Custom or embedded fallback)
  • Method: public boolean isCorrect(String word).

docs.text:
• Pure-Java stateless utility class.
  • Method: public static List<String> split(String identifier).

docs.title: Real-World Case Study: Auditing Checkstyle Core
docs.text: To test the accuracy, performance, and developer utility of checkstyle-spellcheck, we audited the entire **Checkstyle ** codebase (500+ source files in com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle).

docs.title: Key Results & Genuine Bugs Discovered
docs.text: The audit ran in seconds and uncovered 3 genuine grammatical and spelling defects that had existed undetected in core Checkstyle:

docs.title: 1. getThrowed() in JavadocMethodCheck.java:566
docs.text:
• Current Code: private List<ClassInfo> getThrowed() { ... }
  • Defect: Incorrect past tense of the irregular verb throw.
  • Correction: getThrown().

docs.title: 2. getDirectChildsByTag() in XmlMetaReader.java:235
docs.text:
• Current Code: public static List<Element> getDirectChildsByTag(...) { ... }
  • Defect: Incorrect pluralization of the irregular noun child.
  • Correction: getDirectChildrenByTag().

docs.title: 3. isConvertableInInlineTag() in PreferCodeOrSnippetJavadocInlineTagCheck.java:156
docs.text:
• Current Code: private static boolean isConvertableInInlineTag(...) { ... }
  • Defect: Misspelled suffix (-able instead of -ible).
  • Correction: isConvertibleInInlineTag().

docs.title: Performance Profile
docs.text: Metric Result Files Audited 500+ production Java files AST Identifiers Inspected > 100,000 identifier tokens Execution Time < 4 seconds total runtime Cache Hit Ratio > 97% cache hits via wordCache Surviving False Positives 0 after configuring project whitelist.txt

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: IdentifierSpellingCheck is highly configurable, supporting custom whitelists, external dictionaries, and granular AST token selection.

docs.title: Configuration Properties
docs.text: Property Description Type Default Value dictionaryFile Path to a custom Hunspell .dic file. If omitted or blank, uses the embedded default English dictionary. String Embedded en_US.dic affixFile Path to a custom Hunspell .aff file. If omitted or blank, uses the embedded default English affix rules. String Embedded en_US.aff whitelist Path to a project plaintext whitelist file. If omitted or blank, no custom whitelist is applied. String null tokens Tokens to audit. Defaults to all identifier declaration tokens. int[] All 11 declaration tokens

docs.title: Project Whitelist (whitelist.txt)
docs.text:
Every project uses domain-specific acronyms, technical abbreviations, and third-party library names that are not part of standard English dictionaries.

To prevent false positives, point the whitelist property to a plain UTF-8 text file:

<module name="IdentifierSpellingCheck">
  <property name="whitelist" value="config/whitelist.txt"/>
</module>

docs.title: Whitelist Syntax Rules
docs.text:
• One word per line: Trimmed automatically.
  • Case-insensitive: Terms match regardless of capitalization (dto, DTO, Dto).
  • Comments supported: Lines starting with # or // are ignored.
  • Blank lines ignored: Empty lines are safely skipped.

docs.title: Example config/whitelist.txt:
docs.text:
# Domain & Architecture
dto
dao
uuid
uri
regex

# Libraries & Tools
hunspell
checkstyle
sha256
lucene

docs.title: Custom Language / Corporate Dictionaries
docs.text:
To validate identifiers against a foreign language (e.g. German, French) or specialized medical/scientific dictionaries:

<module name="IdentifierSpellingCheck">
  <property name="dictionaryFile" value="config/dictionaries/de_DE.dic"/>
  <property name="affixFile" value="config/dictionaries/de_DE.aff"/>
  <property name="whitelist" value="config/whitelist.txt"/>
</module>

[!NOTE] When providing custom dictionaries, both dictionaryFile and affixFile must be specified together.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Adding checkstyle-spellcheck to your Java project takes just a few lines of configuration.

docs.title: 1. Build Tool Integration
2. Minimal checkstyle.xml
docs.text:
Add IdentifierSpellingCheck under your TreeWalker:

<!DOCTYPE module PUBLIC
    "-//Checkstyle//DTD Checkstyle Configuration 1.3//EN"
    "https://checkstyle.org/dtds/configuration_1_3.dtd">
<module name="Checker">
  <module name="TreeWalker">
    <!-- Zero-config embedded English dictionary -->
    <module name="IdentifierSpellingCheck"/>
  </module>
</module>

docs.title: 3. Running the Audit
docs.text:
Execute your standard build command:

Maven 
mvn checkstyle:check
Gradle 
./gradlew checkstyleMain

docs.title: Tokens & Identifier Splitting
docs.text: Java identifiers rarely consist of single dictionary words. They combine multiple words, abbreviations, and digits following diverse naming conventions.

docs.title: 1. Supported Declaration Tokens
docs.text:
IdentifierSpellingCheck audits all 11 Java declaration AST tokens:

Category Token Example in Java Code Audited Identifier Types CLASS_DEF public class UserAccount UserAccount INTERFACE_DEF public interface OrderRepository OrderRepository RECORD_DEF public record LineRecord(...) LineRecord ENUM_DEF public enum SeasonType SeasonType ANNOTATION_DEF public @interface ServiceAuditor ServiceAuditor Members METHOD_DEF public void printUserName() printUserName VARIABLE_DEF private String userAddress; userAddress PARAMETER_DEF void save(int maxRetryCount) maxRetryCount RECORD_COMPONENT_DEF record Order(String lineItem) lineItem ANNOTATION_FIELD_DEF String defaultName() default ""; defaultName ENUM_CONSTANT_DEF MAX_BUFFER_SIZE MAX_BUFFER_SIZE

docs.title: 2. Identifier Word Splitting Pipeline
docs.text:
IdentifierWordSplitter normalizes complex identifiers through a robust multi-stage pipeline:

flowchart TD
    A["Raw Identifier: 'processSha256Hashe'"] --> B["1. Split by underscores ('_+') and digits ('\\d+')"]
    B --> C["Segments: ['processSha', 'Hashe']"]
    C --> D["2. CamelCase & Acronym boundary regexes"]
    D --> E["Normalized Words: ['process', 'sha', 'hashe']"]
    E --> F["3. Morphological validation against Whitelist & Hunspell"]

docs.title: Supported Naming Styles
docs.text:
• camelCase: userAddress → user, address
  • PascalCase: UserAccount → user, account
  • UPPER_SNAKE_CASE: MAX_BUFFER_SIZE → max, buffer, size
  • Consecutive Uppercase / Acronyms: HTTPServer → http, server; parseJSONResponse → parse, json, response
  • Embedded Digits: sha256Hash → sha, hash; param1 → param
